title: Cavity Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: The cavity thermistor reads open circuit.
fullDescription: Haier countertop and over-the-range microwaves use an NTC sensor in the cavity to monitor temperature during convection and sensor cooking. E-1 is logged when the controller reads the sensor as open. Microwave cooking may be inhibited.

causes.cause: Damaged wire near the cavity grommet

symptoms: Cooking will not start or stops immediately

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the microwave for 5 minutes and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the cabinet only after discharging the high-voltage capacitor. Reseat the sensor connector at the main board.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching Haier cavity sensor and route wire through the original grommet.

whenToCallPro: Microwave high-voltage circuits are dangerous - call a pro if you are not trained in capacitor discharge.

faq.q: Is it safe to open a microwave?
faq.a: No - the high voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge. Discharge it before working inside.

title: Cavity Temperature Sensor Shorted
shortDescription: The cavity thermistor reads short circuit.
fullDescription: Companion code to E-1. The same cavity sensor reads zero ohms (or extremely low resistance), indicating an internal short or wiring shorted to ground. The microwave inhibits cooking until the fault clears.
symptoms: Display shows abnormal high cavity temp

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging the HV cap, inspect the sensor harness for moisture or damage.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure resistance at room temperature. Should be ~50 kOhm. Replace if shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement sensor in the original location.

whenToCallPro: Always advisable for inside-the-cabinet microwave repairs.

faq.a: E-1 is open sensor (no signal), E-2 is shorted sensor (zero resistance).

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: The microwave door switch combination is in an invalid state.
fullDescription: Haier microwaves use multiple interlock switches. E-3 (sometimes shown as DOOR) means the controller sees an inconsistent reading - for example, primary closed but secondary open, indicating a misaligned door, a stuck switch, or a broken latch.

causes.cause: Failed primary or secondary interlock switch

symptoms: Loud snap when closing the door

fixSteps.title: Inspect the door
fixSteps.instruction: Open and close the door slowly. Verify both latch hooks engage and the door sits flush.

fixSteps.title: Replace latch assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If a hook is broken, replace the door latch board and hook assembly with the matching Haier service part.

fixSteps.title: Test interlock switches
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging the HV cap, measure each switch with the door open and closed. Replace any that do not toggle.

whenToCallPro: Replacing the monitor interlock switch should be done by a professional - that switch can fault in a way that arcs the magnetron transformer.

faq.q: Why does the door snap loudly?
faq.a: Often a broken latch hook makes contact with the cabinet rather than the latch board.

title: Humidity / Steam Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The humidity sensor used for sensor cooking is out of range.
fullDescription: On Haier models with sensor cook (popcorn, reheat, vegetables auto-program), a humidity sensor mounted in the exhaust path detects steam. E-4 is logged when the sensor returns an invalid reading.
symptoms: E-4 only when using sensor cook programs
Erratic cook times in auto programs

fixSteps.title: Use manual cooking
fixSteps.instruction: While diagnosing, manual time/power cooking will work normally.

fixSteps.title: Clean the exhaust grille
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the exhaust slots and visible interior of the duct on the back wall to reduce grease loading on the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace humidity sensor
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging HV cap, replace the sensor module on the exhaust duct.

whenToCallPro: Sensor replacement requires opening the cabinet - hire a tech if not trained.

faq.a: Use manual time-and-power cooking to bypass sensor cook entirely.

title: Cavity Overheat Protection
shortDescription: The cavity thermal cutout has tripped due to overheating.
fullDescription: E-5 indicates that the cavity high-limit thermal cutout has opened. This is a safety response to prolonged high temperatures, almost always due to running the microwave empty, blocked vents, or magnetron faults.

causes.cause: Microwave run empty or with very small load

symptoms: E-5 on display, microwave will not start
Strong burnt smell after recent use

fixSteps.title: Allow cool-down
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 30 minutes. Many thermal cutouts auto-reset when cool.

fixSteps.title: Clear the vents
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm exhaust vents on top, bottom, or rear are not blocked by cabinets, towels, or grease buildup.

fixSteps.title: Test the cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging HV cap, verify the cooling fan spins during operation. Replace if stalled.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermal cutout
fixSteps.instruction: If the cutout is permanent and open, replace it with the matching part.

whenToCallPro: If the magnetron is suspected - it requires HV diagnostics.

faq.q: Did running it empty break anything?
faq.a: It can damage the magnetron and door window - inspect carefully before reuse.

title: Convection Heater Fault (OTR/Combi)
shortDescription: The convection heating element is open or not reaching temperature.
fullDescription: On Haier over-the-range and combi microwaves with convection cooking, E-6 reports the convection heater did not reach the expected cavity temperature within the timeout, or the element draws no current.

causes.cause: Failed convection relay on main board

fixSteps.title: Use microwave-only mode
fixSteps.instruction: While awaiting repair, microwave cooking still functions.

fixSteps.title: Test heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging HV cap, measure resistance across the convection element. Open = replace.

fixSteps.title: Test convection fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the convection fan spins during convection mode. Replace if seized.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace heater, fan, or thermal cutout as identified.

whenToCallPro: Convection module repairs typically warrant a service call.

title: Keypad Stuck Button
shortDescription: Touch panel reports a key has been pressed for too long.
fullDescription: F1 is shown when a touch button or membrane key is detected as pressed for over 60 seconds. Often caused by spilled liquid, grease, or a failing membrane.

causes.cause: Liquid or grease on the keypad

symptoms: Buttons respond intermittently or not at all

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes to clear transient faults.

fixSteps.title: Clean the keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe with a barely damp cloth and mild soap. Avoid spraying liquid directly.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging HV cap, reseat the keypad ribbon at the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Install new membrane keypad - typically peel-and-stick over the original substrate.

whenToCallPro: If access requires opening the cabinet near HV components.

faq.q: Why is liquid getting on the keypad?
faq.a: Boil-overs and steam from the cavity can wick into the keypad if the door seal is not maintained.

title: Touch Control Self-Test Failure
shortDescription: The touch control panel failed its power-on self-test.
fullDescription: On Haier capacitive-touch models F3 is reported when the controller does not get a valid handshake from the touch driver IC at power-on. Frequently follows a power surge.
symptoms: Display works but buttons do nothing

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging HV cap, reseat the touch panel ribbon.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch panel
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement touch panel module.

whenToCallPro: Likely best for non-DIYers - HV exposure is involved.

faq.q: Could a surge protector prevent F3?
faq.a: Yes - a quality surge protector reduces the risk of touch IC damage.

title: Inverter Fault (Inverter Models)
shortDescription: The microwave power inverter reported a fault.
fullDescription: Some Haier flagship models use an inverter instead of a high-voltage transformer. F7 is set when the inverter circuit reports overcurrent, overtemperature, or fails its self-check.
symptoms: F7 immediately when start is pressed
Click of relay then immediate fault

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes - some F7 events are transient.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging HV cap, verify the inverter cooling fan spins.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the inverter assembly with the matching Haier service part.

whenToCallPro: Inverter microwaves typically need pro service - parts and replacement may be uneconomical.

faq.a: Often it costs more than half a new microwave. Consider replacing the appliance.

title: Stuck Sensor or Switch
shortDescription: Generic 'sensor error' shown when the controller cannot identify which sensor failed.
fullDescription: SE is a fallback shown on some Haier microwaves when the main board detects a sensor or switch input outside the valid table but cannot localize it. Service mode helps narrow the cause.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clean keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe touch panel with a damp cloth - moisture and grease cause stuck-key faults.

fixSteps.title: Run service mode
fixSteps.instruction: Enter service diagnostics (per service sheet) and read which input is faulted, then service that component.

whenToCallPro: If service mode points to a sensor that requires opening the cabinet near HV components.

faq.q: Is SE the same as Samsung's SE error?
faq.a: The display character is similar but the fault tables differ - always consult the Haier service sheet.
